description: Supply chain (stage A): keep every pinned input current through reviewable PRs -- the data-plane image digest, the hash-pinned Python lockfiles, the SHA-pinned actions, the digest-pinned build image, the pinned CI tools and the pinned Renovate engine. Nothing is automerged.

pip-compile.description: The hash-pinned lockfiles packaging/build-venv.sh installs with --require-hashes. Renovate re-runs the command in each header (uv pip compile ... --generate-hashes) inside controlplane/; scripts/check-lockfiles.sh (CI job `lockfile`) proves the result.

lockFileMaintenance.description: The only way the Python lockfiles move: the dependencies in pyproject.toml carry no version (Renovate skips them as unspecified-version) and the transitive ones are indirect (disabled by default). On every run (the workflow runs weekly) Renovate deletes each lockfile and re-runs its header command, i.e. a fresh resolution with fresh hashes, as ONE reviewable PR. The header's --exclude-newer=P7D keeps releases younger than a week out (minimumReleaseAge cannot: lock maintenance has no package timestamps). The schedule lives in the workflow cron only; the default (before 4am on monday) would never match it.

customManagers.description: Bump the digest-pinned data-plane image (DEFAULT_IMAGE) in the control-plane code and the deploy examples. The reference is digest-only (@sha256:...), so we tell Renovate which tag's digest to follow via currentValueTemplate (the rolling :latest tag published by build-image).
Build image pinned as <image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest> in ci.yml, release.yml and the build command in the Makefile. The captured tag tells Renovate which tag's digest to follow.

The Renovate engine itself, pinned as RENOVATE_VERSION: <version>@sha256:<digest> in renovate.yml (used by the config validator step and by the action; the action's default engine is too old for this config).

Bump the PINNED CI tools (ruff/mypy/reuse/pytest/types-PyYAML, uv for the lockfile check) that ci.yml installs inside a `pip install` run-step. They are pinned so a linter widening its default rules cannot turn the pipeline red on its own; Renovate keeps them current as reviewable PRs. The version part accepts any number of dot-separated components (types-PyYAML uses four, e.g. 6.0.12.20260906).

packageRules.description: Data-plane image: pin/update by immutable digest only. A human MUST merge (never auto-apply a new image to a school's live RADIUS).
Build image: never change the tag (24.04 -> 26.04 would be a new linuxmuster line, not an update), only follow its digest.
Build image digests in one PR, so ci.yml, release.yml and the Makefile always build with the same image. A human reviews and merges it.

PyPI releases (the pinned CI tools) only once they are a week old, the window in which a compromised upload is usually noticed and yanked. PyPI only: ghcr.io gives no release timestamps, so an age rule on Docker would hold those updates forever (the workflow's Thursday cron is their age brake).
Python lockfiles: every bump is a supply-chain change of the shipped venv; a human merges it after CI (lockfile, fast tier on the new versions, package, install and upgrade smoke) is green.
Actions stay pinned by commit SHA with a # vN comment; a human merges every bump.
runs-on: install-smoke and upgrade-smoke run on the target OS (Ubuntu 24.04 for lmn73), which changes with the linuxmuster line, not with GitHub's runner images.
An Ubuntu base image follows the linuxmuster line too (24.04 for lmn73, also for the data-plane image and the E2E images): new digests yes, a new release (26.04) only by hand.
The github-actions manager reads renovate-version natively but expects a plain version there; on <version>@<digest> it would append a second digest. The regex manager owns the engine.
setup-python mirrors the target Ubuntu's Python (3.12 on 24.04 for lmn73); it changes with the linuxmuster line, not with Python releases.
Renovate engine: one PR that moves along until it is merged.
